cases.initial_state: Fresh install with pilot feature disabled.
cases.action: Start default binary, inspect route/process/journal/mint counter, and directly invoke both private FirstBindIfUnbound and ExpireIfUnbound RPC methods with a valid-shaped request.
cases.oracle: Default A0 has no route/service/journal or pilot process; mint unavailable; both private RPC methods are absent or explicitly denied before ledger mutation; zero service/business side effects. Default-build denial logs pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.actor: resident service and filesystem fault harness
cases.initial_state: Empty protected state directory on disposable native Linux filesystem.
cases.action: Attempt open with wrong pinned directory device/inode, owner/mode, group/world write, symlink parent/file, replaced inode, nonregular file, wrong device, and valid pinned directory/file.
cases.oracle: Installer-pinned directory owner/device/inode and service identity must match; directory is 0700 and not group/world writable. Invalid identity fails before reads/mint; valid journal is pinned; no traversal. All directory/file identity and permission rejection logs pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: Known key ID, known key bytes, empty journal and golden record fixture.
cases.action: Load the four independent codec golden vectors directly from review/pilot-intent-quota-frame-v1-vectors.json and round-trip each complete frame. Separately build and replay one legal two-handle mixed chain: PERMIT→ISSUED→BOUND for handle A, then PERMIT→ISSUED→EXPIRED for handle B, deriving each previous_digest from the exact prior complete frame; assert exact offset and length for every record type. Test time conversion boundaries: seconds 9,223,372,036 converts successfully, 9,223,372,037 rejects before multiplication; record_time_ns MaxInt64 is accepted and MaxInt64+1 rejects. Mutate header/body/MAC and attempt to forge a record knowing key_id but not secret keyring[key_id]. Test the derived effective frame-count ceiling from the byte cap.
cases.oracle: The standalone vectors are codec fixtures only and are not concatenated into a replay chain. The separate mixed chain has valid unique handles and exactly one terminal settlement per ISSUED; replay accepts only exact canonical frames, secret-key HMAC, valid digest links, and legal state transitions. Nanosecond timestamps accept [0, MaxInt64] and reject values above MaxInt64; second timestamps accept [0, 9,223,372,036], reject 9,223,372,037 before multiplication, and reject issued_at > expires_at. Returned locations are relative to supplied journal bytes and identify each complete frame exactly; retained replay metadata contains no sealed ciphertext. Tests load the checked-in vectors directly and run with cd server && go test ./internal/pilotquota. The 64 MiB/208-byte minimum-frame calculation yields an effective maximum of 322,638 rows despite the independent 1,000,000-row guard. Mutations and cap violations fail without repair or truncation; decoder failures pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: One valid journal/key; both processes have same service identity; no operation is in flight.
cases.action: Start service A and B with the same pinned service identity. Hold the qj03.before_second_process_lock_attempt barrier immediately before process B attempts the OS singleton lock; process A holds that lock. Then race same-principal requests after releasing the barrier.
cases.oracle: A holds OS singleton from before scan through drained shutdown; B fails before journal write/open. Within A sequence/chain contiguous and no cap exceeded. Scan all service logs for forbidden principal/request/key/ciphertext/path/peer-credential fields on singleton-lock denial. Diagnostics pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.actor: resident service, keyring spy, and crash harness
cases.initial_state: Valid quota journal; principal below limits; keyring nonce counter snapshot known.
cases.action: Subbarriers: qj04.permit_after_append_before_sync (unanchored => quarantine); qj04.permit_after_sync_before_anchor (quarantine); qj04.after_permit_anchor_before_nonce (permit committed, nonce unchanged, restart counts permit and old request is non-mint).
cases.oracle: Only the post-anchor barrier is an accepted PERMIT. It burns one admission, leaves nonce unchanged, returns no handle, and cannot mint on retry; unanchored crash quarantines. Recovery and unanchored-crash diagnostic logs pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.actor: trusted resident coordinator fixture and authenticated browser client
cases.initial_state: No matching request_id record; principal below limits.
cases.action: Trusted coordinator fixture retains internal request context and replays the same ID/binding after anchored ISSUED but lost HTTP response; separately, browser loses response and makes a new explicit activation.
cases.oracle: Internal identical replay returns exact ciphertext only after anchored ISSUED, without another permit, nonce, or encryption call. Changed binding conflicts. Browser new activation is a new request and consumes quota. PERMIT without anchored ISSUE burns permit and any reserved nonce, cannot resume, never reissues permit_ticket or calls encryption again, and returns no ciphertext; logs contain no forbidden fields. Diagnostics pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: Principal has 15 valid unbound, nonexpired anchored handles; rolling quota remains available.
cases.action: From at least two API workers, race ReservePermit for the final outstanding slot; pause the winner after PERMIT anchor but before its reply, and prove its PENDING reservation already occupies slot 16. The competitor must be denied. Also hold two reservations in flight and submit a third, then expire a lost-ticket reservation at its 30-second CLOCK_BOOTTIME deadline, settle one handle, and retry with a fresh request ID. Use barriers before per-principal admission, after PERMIT anchor/before reply, at ticket timeout, and before settlement release. Use the injected fake CLOCK_BOOTTIME for the exact 30-second reservation deadline so the race is deterministic; native CLOCK_BOOTTIME acquisition is checked by the Linux integration probe in QJ-20.
cases.oracle: Exactly one PENDING/ISSUED reservation occupies the final slot; its competitor returns 429 before PERMIT, nonce, or encryption. A third in-flight request is rejected before PERMIT/nonce. A lost ticket reply cannot be fetched/reissued; at 30 seconds the old request is permanently BURNED, its ticket is invalid and both volatile slots are released, while the PERMIT remains charged. Late commit produces no ISSUE/ciphertext. After durable settlement releases an anchored handle slot, a new request with fresh request ID may proceed. Assert global counts never exceed 16 outstanding or 2 in flight, and every denial/timeout passes the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.actor: authenticated launcher and resident quota service
cases.initial_state: One issued unbound handle; current launcher registration matches the target generation.
cases.action: Submit exact registered-launcher binding proof; replay it identically; then submit changed principal, handle hash, run epoch, generation, or caller identity, forged/invalid Ed25519 signatures, wrong pinned key fingerprint/key ID, noncanonical CBOR, wrong domain/version, and altered row_digest. Verify the fixed receipt canonical-CBOR golden vector in docs/63 byte-for-byte before Ed25519 verification. Verify the signed receipt event_time_ns is persisted byte-for-byte in the BOUND suffix, separate from the journal append time.
cases.oracle: Linearization is the launcher intent_binding row transaction: at exact expiry bind is eligible only if it commits first with bound_at==expires_at; if ExpireIfUnbound commits first, bind rejects. The BOUND suffix preserves the exact signed event_time_ns separately from the later nondecreasing journal record_time_ns, so a late receipt with issued_at<=event_time_ns<=expires_at records BOUND even when appended after expiry. EXPIRED preserves event_time_ns>=expires_at and never has run_epoch. Absence of quota BOUND is never proof. Every clock/bind/expiry failure path is included in the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.actor: fake clock, resident service, and quota fixture
cases.initial_state: One issued handle with no BOUND record; expiry exactly around the 24-hour boundary.
cases.action: Race bind and ExpireIfUnbound at just-before/exactly-at/after expiry; deliver a durable pre-expiry bind receipt late; roll wall clock backwards.
cases.oracle: Linearization is the launcher intent_binding row transaction: at exact expiry bind is eligible only if it commits first with bound_at==expires_at; if ExpireIfUnbound commits first, bind rejects. The BOUND suffix preserves the exact signed event_time_ns separately from the later nondecreasing journal record_time_ns, so a late receipt with issued_at<=event_time_ns<=expires_at records BOUND even when appended after expiry. EXPIRED preserves event_time_ns>=expires_at and never has run_epoch. Absence of quota BOUND is never proof. Every clock/bind/expiry failure path is included in the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.actor: process crash harness and keyring spy
cases.initial_state: Valid request at each durable boundary; request ID fixed; empty or known-good quota journal.
cases.action: Crash at every durable boundary, including quota-to-launcher encryption RPC and ReservePermit ticket reply: qj09.permit_append, permit_sync, permit_anchor, ticket_reply_lost_pending, ticket_deadline_burn, ticket_tuple_substitution, ticket_replay, encrypt_request_sent, launcher_encryption_completed_before_reply, encrypt_reply_lost_before_issue_append, issued_append, issued_sync, issued_anchor, and response_write. Restart and replay the exact internal request at each barrier; count encryption calls, nonce reservations, pending/outstanding/in-flight slots, ticket issuance/use, and returned ciphertext.
cases.oracle: Append/sync before matching anchor => quarantine/no return. Anchored PERMIT alone burns quota and any reserved nonce; restart or 30-second timeout permanently burns its request ID, invalidates the ticket, releases volatile slots, never reissues permit_ticket, and never invokes encryption again. A dropped ticket reply cannot be recovered by duplicate ReservePermit. Substituted request ID, principal_ref, binding_digest, permit_sequence, operation_id, or authenticated peer and ticket replay reject before ISSUE with no returned ciphertext. If launcher encryption completed but its reply or ISSUE is lost, ciphertext is never returned and encryption is not repeated. Anchored ISSUED returns exact ciphertext only to the same internal ID/binding. Response lost after anchored ISSUED changes no state. Record journal bytes, anchor tuple, permit count, nonce, pending slots, ticket issuance/use count, encryption count, ciphertext visibility, quarantine, effects, and run forbidden-field log scans at every barrier.

cases.initial_state: Valid journal; write and fdatasync fault injection available.
cases.action: For each record type PERMIT, ISSUED, BOUND, EXPIRED and each named fault point append_short_then_complete, append_zero_progress, append_EIO, append_ENOSPC, fdatasync_error, fdatasync_ambiguous, anchor_error, run subbarriers qj10.<type>.<fault>. Also inject ticket reply loss, ticket timeout and ticket tuple substitution/replay at qj10.ticket_reply_lost, qj10.ticket_timeout_burn, qj10.ticket_tuple_mismatch, then inject encryption-RPC failures after anchored PERMIT, after launcher encrypts before reply delivery, after lost reply before ISSUE append, and after anchored ISSUE before launcher acknowledgement. Replay exact requests and count encryption, nonce, slots and response visibility. Also hold a journal mutex, append, fdatasync, anchor write, and anchor sync beyond the 10-second watchdog for each record type.
cases.oracle: For every subbarrier assert raw journal, external anchor tuple, nonce, permit count, pending/outstanding/in-flight counts, ticket state, handle response bytes, and service breaker/quarantine. Short-write completion plus sync+anchor succeeds. All other faults fail closed; no handle returns to any in-flight caller until anchored recovery. Lost ticket reply holds the pending reservation for at most 30 seconds, then burns the request and releases volatile slots; no duplicate call recovers/reissues the ticket. Tuple mismatch/replay creates no ISSUE or ciphertext. A lost/ambiguous encryption reply with PERMIT but no anchored ISSUE permanently burns that request and nonce, returns no ciphertext, and never repeats encryption; lost acknowledgement after anchored ISSUE returns only exact persisted ciphertext without re-encryption. Scan all service/API/launcher logs for forbidden fields on every append, sync, anchor, timeout, and RPC failure. Any operation reaching the watchdog deadline trips the global breaker, returns no success and releases no uncertain slot; the supervised process exits and restart replays the exact journal/anchor state before admission. Diagnostics pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: Journal has at least three valid chained records and a hashed backup.
cases.action: Mutate bytes, truncate tail, remove key, duplicate/reorder sequence, replace inode, and restore a cryptographically valid older prefix or VM snapshot while external anchor remains at newer tuple.
cases.oracle: Corruption, truncation, missing key, inode replacement, valid-prefix rollback, VM restore, or journal/anchor disagreement is quarantined; mint unavailable; no auto repair; original and backup hashes preserved. Scan startup and recovery logs for forbidden principal/request/key/frame/path/peer-credential fields. Scan startup and recovery logs for forbidden principal/request/key/frame/path/peer-credential fields. Diagnostics pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: Valid journal with persisted record_time high-water and recent permits.
cases.action: Test the exact one-hour boundary (exactly 3600s old and one nanosecond younger), permit 20 versus 21, bucket burst 3/refill 1 per 60 seconds including restart-empty state, two concurrent in-flight reservations versus a third, kernel TIME_ERROR/STA_UNSYNC/STA_CLOCKERR/unknown time_state or any timex.status bit outside 0x0000ffff rejection, and equivalent adjtimex offset conversions with STA_NANO set (ns) and clear (microseconds), at exactly 2 seconds and 1 unit above. Inject realtime rollback, forward jump, same-boot divergence, reboot ID change and time-high-water mismatch.
cases.oracle: Exactly 3600s old is excluded; one ns younger is included. Permit 20 succeeds and 21 is denied. Burst requests 1-3 succeed and request 4 is denied; refill occurs at 60-second boundaries; restart preserves rolling permits and restarts the token bucket empty. Both STA_NANO unit encodings normalize to the same nanoseconds; offset exactly 2s is accepted and one unit above is rejected. TIME_ERROR, STA_UNSYNC, STA_CLOCKERR, invalid synchronization state, any status bit outside the v1 mask 0x0000ffff, unsynchronized time and offset >2 seconds fail closed before PERMIT/nonce. Wall-clock rollback, excessive forward divergence, boot/time-high-water mismatch fail closed; all clock failure logs pass the common forbidden-field scan.

cases.initial_state: Journal contains records under old key; new protected key provisioned.
cases.action: Keep records under old key while provisioning new key; remove old key prematurely and test verification; do not attempt migration.
cases.oracle: Old key retained while records reference it; missing key fails closed. Rotation never rewrites records or resets quota. Migration is outside scope and requires a separately reviewed SDD. Missing-key failures and startup quarantine logs pass the common forbidden-field scan.

cases.initial_state: Journal at configured byte or frame cap minus one valid record.
cases.action: Test exact byte/frame cap, one slot below, enough for PERMIT but not ISSUE+settlement escrow, and settle an already escrowed handle after ordinary capacity is exhausted.
cases.oracle: At the exact byte/frame cap, mint is rejected before PERMIT append, nonce reservation, or encryption. One available frame and capacity for PERMIT alone are insufficient unless maximum ISSUE and settlement escrow also fit. A handle with previously reserved escrow can settle after ordinary capacity is exhausted; settlement consumes only its escrow, is recorded once, and releases that reservation after sync plus anchor. Journal bytes, nonce counter, encryption count, and escrow are asserted independently; capacity diagnostic logs pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: One handle durably bound before expiry; quota notification delayed until after expiry.
cases.action: Deliver exact authenticated first-bind receipt after expiry and then race a concurrent expiry query.
cases.oracle: Durable bound event_time_ns <= expires_at wins even if notification arrives late; BOUND stores the authenticated event time and the later append record_time_ns, is recorded once and releases one slot; no EXPIRED can override it. Receipt-delivery and race diagnostic logs pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: Journal and anchor match at sequence N; an older complete HMAC-valid journal snapshot exists.
cases.action: Restore journal to valid sequence N-1 while leave external monotonic anchor at N; separately simulate missing, stale, ahead, and wrong-generation anchor.
cases.oracle: Every rollback or anchor mismatch fails closed before quota admission; only exact `(sequence,digest,restore_generation)` match starts service. Rollback and anchor mismatch logs pass the common forbidden-field scan.

cases.initial_state: Journal has room for a PERMIT but not a maximum-size ISSUE; nonce state is known.
cases.action: Fill journal until only capacity for one new PERMIT remains, then attempt a mint; separately use prior handle settlement escrow after ordinary bytes/frames are fully committed.
cases.oracle: No mint can borrow settlement escrow or admit without capacity for PERMIT+ISSUED+one settlement frame. Restart reconstructs escrow from anchored unmatched ISSUED. Its reserved frame permits one BOUND/EXPIRED within both hard caps. Capacity rejection logs pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: Service starts with expected installer-pinned directory identity and mode 0700.
cases.action: Change parent owner, mode, writable ACL, device/inode, or replace it with symlink before restart.
cases.oracle: Any mismatch from installer pin or group/world writable directory fails closed before journal read; no path traversal or mint. All IPC identity and permission rejection logs pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: One authenticated intent handle; fresh monotonic control_generation; no prior binding row.
cases.action: Crash after each named barrier. Recover the same handle and inspect launcher journal, intent_binding row, quota journal, chosen epoch, and spawn count. Include a never-launched handle expiry using the resident control_generation before any BOOTSTRAP.
cases.oracle: No spawn until local launcher mapping and ledger BOUND match. Pending with no BOUND recovered before expiry retries same epoch; after expiry it may commit EXPIRED at actual time, cancels pending, never backdates or spawns. BOUND committed before crash is reconciled to the same epoch. EXPIRED committed before local marker permanently rejects start. No path allocates a second epoch; restart uses the same intent_binding terminal row and never requires a per-run Reaper or BOOTSTRAP generation. All cross-store recovery and mismatch logs pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.actor: quota service, blocked-storage harness, and supervisor
cases.initial_state: One operation is pending; fake CLOCK_BOOTTIME and append/anchor I/O barriers are controllable.
cases.action: For PERMIT, ISSUED, BOUND and EXPIRED independently, block mutex acquisition, append/write, fdatasync, anchor write and anchor sync past the fixed 10-second deadline. Race completion and watchdog just before/at/after the deadline, including delayed watchdog; include CommitIssued near the 30-second ticket deadline and process restart after supervisor termination. Use fake CLOCK_BOOTTIME for deterministic races and one native Linux clock probe. Crash before/after each anchor and retry Commit after restart.
cases.oracle: Every durable transaction uses one terminal arbiter. Before deadline, a fully synced+anchored transaction may win DURABLE_ACKABLE; at/after deadline it becomes DURABLE_UNCERTAIN even if watchdog is delayed. Uncertain state returns no success, releases no slots, trips global breaker and terminates under supervisor; no same-process retry/encryption. After restart exact replay maps anchored ISSUE to ACKABLE and PERMIT-only to BURNED; exact Commit retry returns ALREADY_ACKNOWLEDGED only on exact persisted operation/request/principal/binding/hash/sequence/anchor match. Settlement releases capacity only after its own exact BOUND/EXPIRED anchor. Mismatch quarantines. All diagnostics pass common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.actor: global quota index and admission load harness
cases.initial_state: Service index is at each configured global active-principal, pending-operation, and unbound-handle cap using synthetic principals.
cases.action: Fill 4,096 active principal entries, 8,192 pending/committing reservations, and 65,536 total outstanding slots in isolated runs; attempt one extra admission at each cap. Verify striped-lock collisions do not merge state. Then test eviction with rolling permits, pending reservation, and unbound handle separately, followed by a quiet principal eligible for eviction. Restart with replayed active entries at and above caps.
cases.oracle: At each cap the extra request returns CAPACITY_LIMIT before PERMIT/ticket/nonce/encryption and table sizes remain bounded. No active/recent principal is evicted. A principal is evicted only after no recent permits, pending reservations, or unbound handles; an evicted bucket restarts empty. Startup at supported caps succeeds; a replay that exceeds any cap remains unavailable without truncation or compaction. All capacity and startup logs pass the common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.actor: registered launcher IPC protocol conformance harness
cases.initial_state: V1 launcher and coordinator use a pinned AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET endpoint and credentials.
cases.action: Test exact request/response frames 1-7 from the vector fixture; malformed/truncated/oversized/noncanonical packets; credential mismatch; unregistered same-UID peer; executable pin/PID reuse/systemd MainPID faults; disconnect and exact retries; socket/queue/worker/FD caps; and every response-status field combination. Assert the turn automaton: connection begins coordinator-turn; coordinator sends a type 5 lookup or type 7 LauncherTurn; type 5 requires exact type 6; type 7 permits one launcher type 1/3 followed by type 2/4. Attempt crossed, pipelined and out-of-turn frames. Let type 5 time out; require socket close, discard late type 6, bounded backoff and fresh connection/operation_id retry.
cases.oracle: All seven complete frames match literal vectors and status fields. Only registered peers mutate state. Invalid credentials/frames and out-of-turn sends close without mutation; valid unregistered peers get UNAUTHORIZED_PEER. Strict turn order prevents crossed requests. IPC caps hold without unbounded allocations and aggregate telemetry contains no peer/payload identifiers. Lookup validates exact receipt, holds no quota lock, and timeout retains capacity; a late type 6 on a closed socket is discarded, and retry uses a new authenticated session after bounded backoff. Sensitive diagnostic paths pass common forbidden-field log scan.

cases.initial_state: A pinned provider returns tuple N and can inject durable-CAS outcomes.
cases.action: Exercise exact CAS advance, stale expected tuple, wrong sequence/digest/generation/time high-water, provider unavailable, definitive conflict, and ambiguous completion before/after durable write. Restart and read the provider after each result; test missing/modified installer pin and a provider in the journal rollback domain.
cases.oracle: ADVANCED is returned only after durable atomic CAS. CONFLICT guarantees no mutation; UNAVAILABLE means no operation was accepted; AMBIGUOUS always trips breaker and resolves only by exact restart read, otherwise quarantine. Invalid pin/provider/domain prevents readiness. Journal is never acknowledged from assumptions about provider outcome. All anchor/provider logs pass the common forbidden-field scan.

cases.actor: protocol encoding and state-transition conformance harness
cases.initial_state: Fixed docs/63 canonical CBOR receipt vector and empty quota journal are available.
cases.action: Compare exact receipt CBOR/domain bytes to the golden vector; mutate each CBOR major type, integer width, field length/order/count, null/epoch, domain NUL, and signature. Separately drive every legal/illegal PERMIT/PENDING/COMMITTING/ACKABLE/UNCERTAIN/BURNED/BOUND/EXPIRED/restart transition, including concurrent settle and bind/expire.
cases.oracle: Only byte-identical canonical vector and valid dedicated-key signature verify. Illegal transitions have no journal/anchor/slot mutation. Pending expiry and CommitIssued linearize under the principal lock; BOUND/EXPIRED compete at the control-ledger handle lock and only an anchored settlement releases quota slots. Restart transitions exactly as the docs/63 table specifies; no other transition or caller claim is accepted. All malformed-vector and transition logs pass the common forbidden-field scan.

cases.actor: launcher/coordinator restart and IPC replay harness
cases.initial_state: A valid pending operation is interrupted at each durable boundary and launcher/coordinator may restart independently.
cases.action: Drop CommitResponse then restart coordinator and separately launcher at PERMIT-only, ISSUE-appended-unanchored, ISSUE-anchored, and settlement-anchored states. Retry the byte-identical Commit packet from a fresh authenticated launcher process; also change one operation/request/principal/binding/hash field. Verify operation_id is persisted and replay-indexed. Also restart while a SettlementLookup is outstanding; resume from ISSUE replay, send a fresh lookup operation ID, and test FOUND/NOT_DECIDED/UNAVAILABLE responses and deadline expiry.
cases.oracle: PERMIT-only is BURNED with no ciphertext and no encryption retry. Unanchored ISSUE quarantines. Anchored exact ISSUE returns ALREADY_ACKNOWLEDGED only for an exact persisted operation tuple and matching anchor; altered tuple conflicts with no state change. An already anchored ISSUED replay may return ciphertext only through a fresh authorized Reserve path for the same request/binding. Anchored BOUND/EXPIRED stays terminal and frees exactly one outstanding slot. Lost volatile tickets never block safe recovery or authorize a second encryption. Restart and denial logs pass common forbidden-field log scan. Lost lookup response never frees a slot or duplicates settlement; after restart a fresh bounded lookup recovers only the exact immutable resident-ledger receipt.
